expected: Parents can report their child's absence on their phone in about a minute, including the evening before.
explanation: Phone reporting, evening-before reporting and the under-one-minute target are all captured.

expected: The report captures the child, the days and a reason category (sick, doctor's appointment, family reason) without medical details.
explanation: The report captures child, days and a predefined reason category, with no medical details.

expected: Parents receive a confirmation that their report was received.
explanation: A confirmation is shown after the report is submitted.

expected: Parents can request planned absences in advance; up to two days the class teacher approves, longer absences the principal approves.
explanation: Advance requests are covered, with class teacher approval up to two days and principal approval for longer absences.

expected: Parents can see who needs to approve a request and whether it was approved.
explanation: Parents see the approver role and the current status of their request.

expected: Teachers record attendance at the start of each lesson on a tablet in under a minute.
explanation: Attendance is taken per lesson on a tablet in under one minute.

expected: When a child is marked absent without a report from the parents, the school office is alerted so it can call the family.
explanation: The office is alerted about unreported absences and contacts the family.

expected: Absences are visible to the class teacher, to the subject teachers who have the child that day, and as an overview to the school office.
explanation: The class teacher, subject teacher and office views are all specified.

expected: The school office can enter absences reported by phone into the same system.
explanation: The office enters phone-reported absences into the same system.

expected: The number of absences per semester is calculated automatically for the report card.
explanation: Semester absence counts are calculated automatically for the report card.

expected: Parents can be notified if their child does not arrive at school.
explanation: Parents are notified when their child is marked absent without a report.

expected: Information to parents respects custody arrangements and legal restrictions from the canton's student database.
explanation: Custody restrictions from the canton database control what information parents receive.

expected: Students, classes and parents come from the canton's student administration system; no manual entry.
explanation: Master data comes from the canton system and manual entry is excluded.

expected: Health data is protected: no free-text medical information that many people can read.
explanation: There is no free-text or medical reason field, and teachers see only the reason category.

expected: Available in German and English, and ideally Albanian, Portuguese and Tigrinya.
explanation: German and English are required, with Albanian, Portuguese and Tigrinya as candidates.

expected: Report-card totals are kept; daily details are deleted after the school year (to be confirmed).
explanation: Report-card totals are kept, daily details are deleted after the school year, and this is still to be confirmed.

expected: Retention periods need to be confirmed with the canton's data protection officer.
explanation: Retention periods are raised as a question for the canton data protection officer.

expected: How does the interface to the student administration system work? (Ask the canton's IT department.)
explanation: The interface question is addressed to the canton IT department.

expected: Success: the school knows about every missing child within 30 minutes of the first lesson.
explanation: The thirty-minute detection target is stated, and the summary names missing children as the main risk.
